column1: # tools/uspacescan-names.tsv -- the names R7 forbids, the ones it allows, and
# the two that exist only to make the instrument show its hand.
# This file is DATA on purpose: `tools/uspacescan.py` keys nothing off an
# individual name, so the gate's subject can be widened or narrowed without
# touching the instrument -- and `test-uspacescan.sh` D1 proves the table is
# load-bearing by moving `execve` to FORBIDDEN in a copy of this file and
# requiring the verdict on the very same ELF to flip.
# class     FORBIDDEN  its presence in the artefact is a finding; the gate fails
#           ALLOWED    counted and printed on every run, never flagged
#           CONTROL    not part of the verdict; its `expect` must hold or the
#                      tool refuses to report anything at all
# expect    only read for CONTROL rows
#           ZERO   both sources must report 0 occurrences
#           NOFP   source (1) must report "no fingerprint could be built", i.e.
#                  UNDECIDED -- the proof that an unfingerprintable name comes
#                  back undecided and never as a passing 0
# The dividing line between FORBIDDEN and ALLOWED is NOT "does it start a
# process".  It is "can the bytes that decide WHAT runs be a string something
# else parsed":
#   system, popen          hand the whole command line to /bin/sh -c
#   execl, execle          argv arrives as varargs, which is how a caller that
#                          meant to build an array ends up building "sh -c ..."
#   execlp, execvp         search PATH, so the file that runs is decided by the
#                          environment rather than by the program
#   execve, fork, vfork    argv is an array the caller built from typed values,
#                          the path is absolute, and nothing is searched
# name
system
column4: the whole command line is parsed by /bin/sh -c

column1: popen
column4: the whole command line is parsed by /bin/sh -c

column1: execl
column4: varargs argv; the usual carrier of a built-up command line

column1: execlp
column4: varargs argv, and PATH decides which file runs

column1: execvp
execle
column4: varargs argv with a caller-supplied environment

column1: execve
column4: typed argv array, absolute path, no PATH search, no shell

column1: fork
column4: makes a process; decides nothing about what it runs

column4: makes a process; decides nothing about what it runs
